explanations.explanation: Joshua son of Nun, standing right there beside Moses. The LORD had commissioned him to bring the Israelites into the land (Deuteronomy 31:23). So one man recites the song and the other man is about to do the walking. You nailed it, baker.

Caleb son of Jephunneh was one of the men Moses sent to spy out Canaan (Numbers 13:2, 6), so I see why he came to mind. But Deuteronomy 32:44 names a different man beside Moses. It's Joshua son of Nun, the one the LORD commissioned to bring Israel into the land (Deuteronomy 31:23). Caleb will have to wait for another passage.

Eleazar was Aaron's son (Numbers 20:28), so he's a fair guess from this family tree. But the verse says Moses came with Joshua son of Nun. Joshua is the one the LORD commissioned to bring the Israelites into the land (Deuteronomy 31:23). Eleazar didn't get a mention in this verse, and I bet he's fine with that.

explanations.answer: So they can command their children to follow the law
explanations.explanation: Moses says, "Take to heart all the words I have solemnly declared to you this day, so that you may command your children to carefully follow all the words of this law." The words are meant to be passed on from parents to children. That's a whole line of people carrying one message. Good catch, baker.

explanations.answer: So they can teach the law to the nations nearby
explanations.explanation: That's a reasonable guess, but Moses doesn't mention the nations nearby here. He says they should take his words to heart so that they may command their children to carefully follow the law. The message stays in the family first. I'd say Moses is thinking about the next generation.

explanations.answer: So they can carve the law on the city gates
explanations.explanation: Carving sounds very official, I'll give you that. But Moses says nothing about gates or carving in these verses. He says to take his words to heart so that they may command their children to carefully follow all the words of this law. The target is the children, not the stonework.
Moses says, "…they are not idle words to you, because they are your life…" Not a nice extra and not a side dish. It's their life. You read that one just right, baker.

History is a good word, and a song can hold plenty of it. But Moses gives a different reason: "…they are your life…" He doesn't call the words their history. He says the words are their life, which is a much bigger claim.
Pride is a fun guess, friend, but it's not what Moses says. His reason is, "…because they are your life…" Nothing in the verse is about Israel feeling proud. The words are about living.

True. Moses says, "…by them you will live long in the land that you are crossing the Jordan to possess." The land is across the river, and the words are tied to living long there. Sharp reading, baker.

This one is actually true, friend, and I get why it sounded too good. Moses says, "…by them you will live long in the land that you are crossing the Jordan to possess." The words are their life, and by them they will live long in the land across the Jordan. Keep that verse in your pocket.
Nebo it is. The LORD says to go up into the Abarim Range to Mount Nebo, in the land of Moab across from Jericho. That's a very specific address, and you caught it. Well done, baker.

Sinai is a famous mountain for Moses. The LORD came down on Mount Sinai and called him up to the top (Exodus 19:20). But in this passage the LORD sends him to a different mountain, Mount Nebo in the Abarim Range. Same man, new climb.

Carmel is a real mountain, where the prophet Elijah later stood against the prophets of Baal (1 Kings 18:20). But that's far from this scene. Here the LORD tells Moses to go up into the Abarim Range to Mount Nebo, in the land of Moab across from Jericho. Carmel will get its turn with Elijah, friend.

View is the word. The LORD says, "…view the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the Israelites as their own possession." Moses is sent up there to look at it. It's a big view of a big gift, and you got it.

Blessing is a lovely thing to do on a mountaintop, but it's not the word here. The LORD tells Moses to "view the land of Canaan." The land is the thing He is giving to the Israelites as their own possession. Moses is sent up to look at it.

Dividing sounds like a job with a clipboard. But the LORD doesn't give Moses that task in this verse. He tells him to "view the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the Israelites as their own possession." On this mountain, Moses looks.

explanations.answer: He will die and be gathered to his people
explanations.explanation: That's what the LORD says: "…there on the mountain that you climb, you will die and be gathered to your people…" It's a heavy part of the passage, friend, and I think it's worth moving through gently. You read it right, baker.

explanations.answer: He will be taken up into heaven alive
explanations.explanation: That's a big, dramatic guess, but it isn't what the LORD tells Moses. He says, "…there on the mountain that you climb, you will die and be gathered to your people…" It's a hard word, and I think it was hard to hear. The text gives us exactly what it gives us.

explanations.answer: He will stay there and pray for Israel
explanations.explanation: Praying for Israel is a good thing to picture, but this verse doesn't say it. The LORD tells Moses, "…there on the mountain that you climb, you will die and be gathered to your people…" That's the whole of what He says about the mountain. I think it's a heavy part, baker.
Aaron it is. The LORD says Moses will die there "just as your brother Aaron died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his people." Two brothers, two mountains. You caught it, baker.

Miriam was Moses' sister, and she did die in the wilderness, at Kadesh (Numbers 20:1). But the LORD points to someone else here, and to a mountain. He says, "…just as your brother Aaron died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his people."

Amram was the father of Moses and Aaron (Exodus 6:20), so family was a smart place to look. But the LORD names a different relative here. He says, "…just as your brother Aaron died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his people." It's a brother, not the father.

The LORD actually says it the other way around. He says, "…both of you broke faith with Me among the Israelites…" Both of them, Moses and Aaron, at the waters of Meribah-kadesh in the Wilderness of Zin. It's an easy one to slide past, friend.

False, because the LORD says, "…both of you broke faith with Me among the Israelites by failing to treat Me as holy in their presence." That means Moses and Aaron, together, at Meribah-kadesh. The LORD names the place, the two men and what happened. Good work, baker.

I know that's the happy ending we'd all like, friend. But the LORD says, "Although you shall see from a distance the land that I am giving the Israelites, you shall not enter it." Moses gets the view, and he doesn't get to walk in. I think this is a hard line to read.

False. The LORD says, "Although you shall see from a distance the land that I am giving the Israelites, you shall not enter it." Moses will see the land and the Israelites will receive it. It's a hard line, and you read it right, baker.
